job.style: a description of a classroom activity or experiment and what it shows

response.passage: Today in our science class, we examined various food packets to understand how to read labels correctly. We started by looking at a box of cookies that claimed 'No added sugar' on the front, but the ingredient list clearly showed 'maltose' and 'fruit juice concentrate', which are forms of sugar. We learned that the first ingredient listed is always the one present in the largest quantity by weight. Next, we compared two packets of snacks. One had a green dot, confirming it is vegetarian, while the other had no mark at all. Our teacher explained that a missing mark does not automatically mean a product is vegetarian; one must always check the full ingredient list. We also discussed the FSSAI logo, which is a regulatory mark indicating that the food meets safety standards, not necessarily that the product is 'healthy' or nutritious. Finally, we looked at a bottle of juice with a 'Best Before' date. We learned that 'Best Before' indicates the quality and freshness period, whereas an 'Expiry' date indicates the point after which food may become unsafe to consume. We concluded that reading the fine print is essential for making informed choices, as marketing claims on the front of the pack can often be misleading.
response.summary: This activity teaches students to look beyond marketing claims on food packaging. It highlights the importance of reading ingredient lists and understanding regulatory marks to make informed dietary choices.

options.why: Student thinks the first ingredient is the smallest amount.
Student confuses ingredient weight with fat content.
Student assumes the first ingredient is always sugar.

items.stem: How can you be certain about the vegetarian status of a food item that lacks a green dot?

Student thinks eggs are vegetarian and don't need marks.
Student thinks only the word sugar matters.

items.stem: What is the primary purpose of the FSSAI logo on a food package?

options.why: Student equates safety certification with being healthy.
Student thinks the logo implies low fat content.
Student thinks the logo confirms daily nutrient needs.
